question: Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty (DMEK) offers faster visual rehabilitation and better final visual acuity than DSAEK, but has a higher rate of graft detachment (rebubbling rate).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. DMEK = faster vision + better acuity but higher rebubbling rate. DSAEK = thicker graft (includes stromal layer), slower vision recovery, lower rebubbling risk. Both treat endothelial disease (Fuchs', bullous keratopathy).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. DMEK (Descemet membrane only, no stroma) → thinner graft → faster visual recovery, superior BCVA (often 6/6). However, DMEK has a higher rebubbling rate (~35% vs ~5% DSAEK) due to the tendency of the thin graft to scroll. Trade-off: speed/vision vs. technical ease.
